summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, spread over three disk sides, that won the C64 demo compo at X 2008 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2008.
why: Sceners praise its polish, the flow between parts, the vector work and Dane's soundtrack. Several describe it as a demo that keeps growing on you with repeat viewings.

quote.text: Now, after having watched it countless times, I can safely say that I am blown away.

summary: Batman Group's Amstrad CPC demo, which won the CPC demo compo at Forever 2011 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2011.
why: It also took Best Technical Achievement and Public Choice at those awards, and was nominated for Best Graphics and Breakthrough Performance. Tagged as using the Batman theme.

summary: Oxyron's two-disk-side C64 demo, the thirteenth Coma Light, which won the demo compo at X 2012. Code is by Axis, Peiselulli and Bitbreaker, music by Fanta.
why: Sceners single out Fanta's soundtrack and samples, the parallax part, the vectors with balls and the perspective scroller, and many rank it among the best C64 demos.

quote.text: I love everything about this demo, but one thing really stands out for me - the sound, music and samples.

summary: Resource and Chorus's three-disk-side C64 demake of the Amiga demo Desert Dream, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: Sceners admire how close the effects get to the Amiga original, with Fanta's soundtrack fitted to three SID voices. Opinion on remakes was split, but the effort behind it was widely praised.
highlights: Amiga tunes on three SID voices

quote.text: Amazing that a large number of the effects actually look VERY close to the original, guess it shows the power of the C64 in the hands of the right coders!

summary: Logon System's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2017. Code and graphics are by Overflow, music by Tom&Jerry.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2018. The source is available for anyone who wants to see how it was done.

summary: lft's 256-byte C64 intro with music, which won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2017. lft did both the code and the music.
why: Sceners are amazed at fitting a tune and a glitchy visual show into 256 bytes. lft's detailed writeup on his website is praised too, and it was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2018.

quote.text: This is the way to steal a show -- do something nobody has seen in as few bytes as possible.

summary: Glance's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2010.
why: Sceners praise the smooth vectors and the variety of effects, and one calls it a technical milestone. A themed design and an extensive note file on the disk also get mentioned.

quote.text: A thoroughly enjoyable demo with non stop action and varied effects.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2003. Viznut did the code, graphics and music, with graphics from ccr.
why: Tagged as using speech synthesis, and Viznut handled the code, graphics and music himself.

summary: Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights' demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4, which won the Alternative Platforms Demo compo at Evoke 2014.
why: A win on a less common platform. It features the picture Meanmachine by Nero and uses Krill's loader, and the tags say it runs in an endless loop.

summary: Condense's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. NoRecess did the code, CeD the graphics and Aki the music.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2019. The source and a writeup are both available.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at X 2010. It is dedicated to the memory of Jerry/Triad and Sammi Hoyt Barakat.
why: Sceners single out the scrolling panda picture, the parallax landscape and the soundtrack, with tunes by Danko, Abaddon and Magnar. It was also nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

quote.text: I love the humongous scrolling pictures (panda, endpart).

summary: Instinct and Booze Design's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2009 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009.
why: Sceners single out the long 3D section, the recursive zoomer, Archmage's graphics and Dane's minimalistic soundtrack, which was kept lean to leave rastertime for the effects.

quote.text: State of the art, innovative demo effects here.

summary: Aeon is a ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, which won the Combined Low-End compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2008.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2008. Graphics are by pROF, with animation by G.D. and music by Key-Jee.

summary: Booze Design's two-disk-side C64 demo, entered at X 2014 as The Booze Demo, where it came second. It carries a political message and uses X-FLI.
why: Sceners single out the rotating raster bars, with some calling it the best C64 effect so far. The fractal zoomer, palette rotators and the demo's message are also mentioned.

quote.text: the rotating rasters was the best effect!

summary: Censor Design and Oxyron's four-disk-side C64 collaboration, the party version of which won the demo compo at X 2014. The name fuses Oxyron's Coma Light and Censor's Wonderland series.
why: Sceners single out the textured cube, the scrolling intro picture, the graphics and logos, and the massive credits part. The mix of styles from so many contributors sparked a long debate about coherence.

quote.text: The demo features some of the nicest demo gfx and logos ever made and some really solid code.

summary: lft's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2016. He did the code, graphics and music himself.
why: Sceners praise how the rain-soaked story, the minimalistic art and the music hold together, and that it is all the work of one person. It earned four Meteoriks 2017 nominations, including Best Storytelling.

quote.text: I love how the parts are connected by the story and how well the music bridges the parts and holds them together (the rain scenes are crazy good).

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC 4K intro, which won the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2018. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Tom&Jerry the music.
why: A compo win in the 4K class on the CPC. The tags mark it as isometric and set to loop endlessly.

summary: Chiphead is an Atari VCS 2600 demo by KK of Altair, which won the Atari VCS 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. KK did all the code.
why: Nominated for the That's Not Possible On This Platform award at The Meteoriks 2017. Tagged as a demake with dance animations and a rave theme.

summary: Smash Designs and The Obsessed Maniacs' two-disk-side C64 remake of the PC demo Second Reality, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1997.
why: Sceners rate kb's SID soundtrack highly, and one thinks it beats the original's music. Views on the conversion's execution are mixed, but it remains a favourite for people who know the original.

quote.text: The music in this remake is incredible, particularly part 4.

summary: Reflex's two-disk-side C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1995. PVCF did the music, with code by Guru, kb and Quiss.
why: Sceners remember it as the demo that showed PC-style effects such as rotating tunnels running on a C64, and for PVCF's techno-influenced tunes. It was voted third best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: I was absolutely blown away with the PC style effects, it was just a total revelation to see that rotating tunnels etc. could be done on the C64.

summary: Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights' demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4, which won the Commodore 8bit Demo compo at Revision 2011.
why: Mad did the code, Degauss the code and music, Nero the 2D graphics and Decca the fonts. It uses Krill's loader.

summary: Numen is an Atari 8-bit demo by Taquart, which won the demo compo at Lato Ludzików 2002. Fox and Eru did the code, Dracon the graphics and X-Ray the music.
why: The tags list bump mapping, Phong shading, a cube, a torus, a Rubik's cube, a dancer and Einstein, so it is packed with 3D and shading work for an 8-bit machine.

summary: Bold is an MSX demo by Dvik and Joyrex, which won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2009. Moran composed the music.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. The video title also bills it as the winner of that party.

summary: SHizZLE is a demo by Team Pokeme for the Pokemon Mini, which won the wild demo compo at Breakpoint 2005.
why: The video title says it runs on real Pokemon Mini hardware. The fact sheet has no credits or tags beyond that, so this is a short entry.

summary: Oxyron's C64 sequel to Natural Wonders, which came second in the C64 demo compo at X 2008. Axis wrote the code, with music by Fanta and Kasmo and graphics by Oys and Yazoo.
why: Sceners single out how the music is synced to the parts, including filters that dim as black shapes cover the pictures. The vector effects, transparent balls and the greetings end part also get praise.

quote.text: I like the way how Fanta's audio track has been fitted to the parts. Definately the best synchronising to date!

summary: Oxyron and Crest's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. It has a hidden part and a notefile with exact credits for each part.
why: Sceners praise its design, polished presentation and music, and many call it the demo to show people new to the C64. It features pictures by Cyclone and DeeKay that placed in the party's graphics compo.

quote.text: Still one of the best demos, and one of the best demo soundtracks ever, if not THE best.

summary: A three-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Pal did the graphics, with music by several composers including Scarzix and Wiklund.
why: Sceners single out the hires graphics used throughout, the long scrollers and the soundtrack. It was made as a tribute to the people who organise Datastorm.

quote.text: Such a beautiful demo full of outstanding graphics, music and code.

summary: Phantasy's Game Boy demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Dalton did the code, Exocet the graphics and zabutom the music.
why: A podium finish on the Game Boy, with music played by a Carillon player according to the tags.

summary: Weed is a ZX Spectrum demo by Triebkraft, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CAFe 2003.
why: The fact sheet gives no credits or tags, so the compo win is all there is to say.

summary: Mona is a 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit, who did all the code. The video title gives its size as 250 bytes.
why: Its Demozoo note points to a code golf thread titled Let's draw Mona Lisa, where it has been ported to many different programming languages.

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2012. Groepaz and Peacemaker did the code, with music by Dane and graphics by Pal, Nerdine and Peacemaker.
why: Sceners value its mood and art over raw tech, and Dane's somber soundtrack. The credits tree, the fire routine and the mix of hires and multicolour are often mentioned. It marked a Hitmen comeback.

quote.text: To me, it's already a classic, seems to get better and better the more often I watch - and listen to!

summary: Fairlight and Instinct's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Backslash 2007 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007.
why: Sceners single out the growing-branches opening, the pipe effect and the clean, hires, full frame rate effects. Goto80's experimental soundtrack divided opinion.

quote.text: the growing branches and the triangle head over blue and purple backdrop, has to be the most original demo part i have seen in ages.

summary: CyberPunk is an Atari 8-bit demo by Lamers, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Ajcek and Szeryf did the code, with music by Wieczor.
why: The tags mark it as a cyberpunk-themed demo using speech synthesis and 256k.

summary: Gejmbåj is a Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with code and graphics by Snorpung and music by Nordloef. The video was captured on a real Game Boy Pocket.
why: Nominated for Breakthrough Performance and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2010. Tagged as 2mbit and set to loop endlessly.

summary: From Scratch is an Amstrad CPC demo by Vanity, with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and music by Tom&Jerry. The video title describes it as 50Hz and 4k.
why: Nominated for Public Choice at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as a plasma demo.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Floppy 2004. It loops endlessly and has three alternative soundtracks, and the tags call it scene poetry.
why: Sceners praise its stylish design, the flow of fades between parts and Dane's music, which one comment says plays at four times speed. Several name it as their favourite Booze demo.

quote.text: The transitions are not too short or too long, the pace is perfect.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Ultrasyd the music.
why: The tags list a kaleidoscope, plasma zoom, rotozoomer, twister and zoom scroller. It also includes a Pulpo Corrosivo cracktro coded by Toms.

summary: In The Future is a ZX Spectrum demo by Hooy-Program, which came second in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2016. Gasman did the code, graphics, music and lyrics.
why: Tagged as karaoke, with the lyrics written by Gasman himself. It was nominated for Best Storytelling at The Meteoriks 2017.
highlights: Written, drawn and scored by Gasman

summary: High Hopes is a NES demo by Aspekt, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007. Ruuvari did the code, graphics and music, with code and design from thefox.
why: A compo win on the NES, made by just two people according to the credits.

summary: KPACKU Deluxe is a ZX Spectrum demo by Kpacku, which won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015. Trefi did the code and prof4d and Tutty the graphics.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2016. Tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode and 128K.

summary: Mescaline Synesthesia is a ZX Spectrum demo by deMarche, which won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2009.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as using multicolour mode and 128K.

summary: UnMEC is an Atari 8-bit demo by Agenda, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. xeen, Pr0be, Koala and Svoy share the code.
why: It won Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2017. Music is by stRing and Caruso, graphics by Piesiu, Ooz and Ripek.

summary: Syntax Infinity is an MSX demo by Tulou and Traktor, which placed fifth in Console/Real Wild at Breakpoint 2009. Esau did code, graphics and music.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as MSX2.

summary: Plush's C64 4K intro, which won the 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2006. Krill wrote the code and Fanta the music, and the source is available.
why: Sceners single out the voxel landscape and the rotating planet, and many call it one of the best 4Ks. Krill released the source and tools so others could reuse the ideas.

quote.text: it has impressive, although PCish effects (nicest voxel landscape I've seen on c64 at least).

summary: Break Space is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2016. The credits list a dozen contributors across code, graphics and music.
why: The credits name a dedicated 3D engine by X-Trade, plus 3D modelling and 2D animation, which suggests a 3D-heavy production.

summary: Byterapers' C64 demo, the third Follow The Sign, which won the C64 demo compo at Assembly 1996. Mr. Sex did the code and AMJ the music. The party version is known as the 75% version.
why: Sceners praise AMJ's fast-paced soundtrack, the voxelspace routine and the blocky effects, and note how smoothly the parts flow. It was voted 17th best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: This is one of the best blocky-effects demos out there. Never boring and great music.

summary: Error 23 is a C64 demo by The Dreams and Resource, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2006 and won Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2006.
why: Sceners single out the bump mapper, the rubber vector over Leon's picture and the horizontal twister. The party version was unfinished, which several commenters regret.

quote.text: i didnot think i would be impressed by a bump mapper again, but this one was extremely good looking.

summary: Egypt, 2600 BC is an Atari VCS demo by Genesis Project, which won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17. Shadow did the code, Mermaid the music and graphics.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018.

summary: Triad's two-disk-side C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017. Flex was a guest musician, and the code is shared between five coders.
why: Sceners love its 1980s neon look, with a grid, sports cars and venetian blind fades, plus the glowing raster bars and Flex's soundtrack. It was nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018.

quote.text: This is the demo that got me fully hooked on C64 demos - tons of style, so much feeling, and a Flex soundtrack to die for.

summary: I am the seed is a ZX Spectrum demo by Inward and Cyberpunks Unity, which came second in the 8 Bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2005. Elfh did the code and text.
why: Nominated for Best Effects and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2005. Moran did graphics, and Miguel did graphics and music.
